voting.auth.code.description.t: Some elections provide voters with a personal voting code — usually sent by the election administrator by email, post, or in person. If you received such a code, enter it here to go directly to the ballot.

voting.auth.code.failed.t: Could not sign in with that voting code. Please check the code and try again.

voting.auth.email.description.t: If the election administrator has your email address on file, enter it here. We will send a one-time code to that address. Enter the code on the next screen to confirm your identity and access the ballot.

voting.auth.email.sendFailed.t: Could not send a verification code to that email address.

voting.auth.faq.a1.t: To protect the integrity of the election, we need to confirm that each voter is who they say they are, and that they are on the list of eligible voters. This prevents anyone from voting more than once or on someone else's behalf.

voting.auth.faq.a2.t: The information you enter must match exactly what the election administrator registered for you. If it isn't recognised, please contact the election administrator — they can verify your details or provide you with a personal voting code instead.

voting.auth.faq.a3.t: Yes, absolutely. This sign-in step only confirms that you are an eligible voter. Once you are on the ballot page, your choices are completely private. The system is designed so that no one — not even the election administrators — can link your name to the specific choices you made.

voting.auth.faq.a4.t: No. Once you have submitted your ballot, the system records that you have voted and will not accept a second submission from you. This is an important safeguard for election integrity.

voting.auth.faq.a5.t: You can use any one of the available methods — you don't need to use all of them. If you have an email address on file with the election, use the Email option. If you have a phone number, use the Phone option. If you received a personal code, use the Code option. Contact the election administrator if you are unsure which method applies to you.

voting.auth.faq.a6.t: Yes. Signing in with Google means Google confirms your identity to us — we never see your Google password. We only receive your verified email address, which we check against the voter list. Google provides this service at no charge.

voting.auth.faq.a7.t: Please contact your election administrator directly. They can check your registration details, provide a personal voting code, or assist you in any other way.

voting.auth.welcome.detail.t: This is a simple one-time check — we're not creating an account for you or storing any personal information beyond what the election administrator already has. Once confirmed, you'll be taken directly to the ballot.

voting.auth.welcome.intro.t: In order to vote in this election, we need to confirm who you are. Your identity must match the information that the election administrator has on file for eligible voters.
